correctness.rationale: Local P1 mass matrices and the original multiplicity scaling give exact SPD block formulas. Two explicit independent eigenvectors have eigenvalue one; a (k-2)-dimensional subspace has eigenvalue 4/3 for unequal arms; trace and continuity determine the remaining eigenvalue mu=4ST/(3k^2). Jacobi diagonal similarity yields eigenvalues 1/2,1 repeated,3/2. Cauchy–Schwarz and an attainable Kantorovich bound prove the universal exact crossover. A standard-library checker independently reassembled 53 exact-rational star instances and three boundary/exemplar instances, verifying both characteristic polynomials, plus exact eigenvector identities. Diagnostics support but do not substitute for the uniform algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: The original method and general projector bound belong to Krzysik–Southworth–Wimmer (arXiv:2607.12138, 2026-07-13). The newly evaluated complete spectrum on stars of any degree and arbitrary positive arm lengths, and its sharp universal Jacobi comparison, are not equivalent to the generic projector-norm reformulation, the classical Kantorovich bound, or the previously documented alternating cycle. Actual direct primary sections, published-source searches, exact-formula queries and relevant comparison records produced no identified covering statement. This is a qualified best-knowledge originality assessment; inaccessible full texts and seminar slides remain specific risks.

value.rationale: The full arbitrary-degree, arbitrary-arm star spectral classification is a natural complete structural invariant for an important algebraic local-inverse preconditioner. Its computed arithmetic–harmonic statistic gives a sharp universal mesh-grading safeguard against a fixed Jacobi condition number, with a concrete four-branch counterexample past the threshold. This is relevant to deciding when multiplicity averaging can be ineffective on graded network meshes, beyond existing periodic two-length analyses; it is not a mere table entry or unmotivated parameter slice.
